identity.name: Communist Party of China (Chinese Soviet Republic, Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region and Liberated Areas)
native_names: 中华苏维埃共和国 (Zhōnghuá Sūwéi'āi Gònghéguó)

land.text: the Jiangxi-Fujian soviet area of the predecessor row plus a 100 km circle at Ruijin (116.03 E, the capital), which lies outside Cliopatria's 1930-1931 shape (it ends at 115.28 E)

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's two rows share Wikidata Q17427; they are one continuing party-state. The chinese-communists dossier (ea-08-c) ends on 7 November 1931 with this one as successor, handing over the same region (its ledger 2); this row begins in Cliopatria in 1932. [repair 2026-10-25] The land now includes a 100 km circle at Ruijin, which Cliopatria's 1930-1931 shape misses.

land.text: the other soviets the page names as territories of the Republic (Minzhegan, Xianggan, Xiang'egan, Honghu, Xiang'echuanqian, Eyuwan, Eyushan, Shaanxi-Gansu, Sichuan-Shaanxi, Hailufeng): Cliopatria's 1932 shape outside the Jiangxi-Fujian core

predecessors.note: [repair 2026-10-25] The Republic was proclaimed on 7 November 1931 over soviets that already stood in Hubei, Henan, Anhui, Hunan, Zhejiang, Guangdong, Sichuan, Shaanxi and Gansu (Chinese Soviet Republic page, closely paraphrased); the land was nominally the Nationalist Republic's. The republic-of-china dossier (ea-08-c) has no matching loss: see the notes.

land.text: Shanxi: most of the province in 1948, Taiyuan and Datong on 24 April 1949 and after (Taiyuan campaign page)

predecessors.note: [repair 2026-10-25] The shanxi-clique dossier (ea-08-x) loses most of Shanxi to this state in 1948 (its ledger 9) and dissolves into it in April 1949 (its ledger 10); the ledger here mirrors both.

land.text: the communist-held land at the proclamation of 1 October 1949: north and northeast China, Shandong, Henan, Shanxi, the lower Yangtze south to Nanjing

successors.note: 'On 1 October 1949, Mao Zedong officially proclaimed the People's Republic of China (PRC) with its capital at Beiping.' The conquest of the south and west (Guangzhou, Chongqing, Chengdu) follows in the people-s-republic-of-china dossier.

capitals.name: Ruijin
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Ruijin, Jiangxi Soviet (1931-1934)'; the infobox gives the fall of Ruijin as 10 November 1934. No gazetteer entry for Ruijin.

capitals.name: Bao'an (Zhidan)
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Bao'an, Yan'an Soviet (1936-1937)'; the Second Red Army 'reached Bao'an (Shaanxi) on October 22, 1936' (Long March). No gazetteer entry.

capitals.name: Yan'an
capitals.note: The CCP headquarters was established in Yan'an in January 1937 (Shaan-Gan-Ning page, closely paraphrased). The KMT seized Yan'an in March 1947; the pages opened do not say where the leadership sat from then to 1949. No gazetteer entry.

capitals.name: Beiping (Beijing)
capitals.note: 'Mao Zedong officially proclaimed the People's Republic of China (PRC) with its capital at Beiping' on 1 October 1949; the page does not date the Party centre's move there.

correction.text: the soviets the Chinese Soviet Republic was proclaimed over on 7 November 1931, with Ruijin: Cliopatria's 1932 'Communist Party of China' shape used for 1931 (confidence 2), because the page lists the Minzhegan, Xianggan, Xiang'egan, Honghu, Xiang'echuanqian, Eyuwan, Eyushan, Shaanxi-Gansu, Sichuan-Shaanxi and Hailufeng soviets as the Republic's territories

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Communist Party of China row begins in 1932 but the Chinese Soviet Republic was proclaimed on 7 November 1931 by Mao Zedong and Zhu De. [repair 2026-10-25] The first draft drew the predecessor row's 1930-1931 shape (38,942 km2, 168 cells, bbox 113.58-115.28 E): it does not contain the capital Ruijin (116.03 E) and leaves out the other soviets, so nothing in the ledger explained the jump to the 1932 shape (297,451 km2, 1,330 cells) a year later. The Chinese Soviet Republic page lists the Minzhegan, Xianggan, Xiang'egan, Honghu, Xiang'echuanqian, Eyuwan, Eyushan, Shaanxi-Gansu, Sichuan-Shaanxi and Hailufeng soviets as its territories, says 'the second-largest soviet, in Eyuwan, failed to send delegates' to the Ruijin conference, and says soviets were created from 1929 on, so they stood in November 1931; the 1931 outline is therefore Cliopatria's 1932 shape (it contains Ruijin: 12 cells within 30 km), as the core (ledger 0) plus the other soviets (ledger 1). Area: the page's 'approximately 70,000 square kilometers' is for the 1933 peak; 297,451 km2 is 4.25 times it (see the 1932 keyframe).

correction.text: unchanged shape, but it holds for 1932-1934 only: the Jiangxi Soviet is abandoned from October 1934 and Ruijin falls in November 1934 (10 November, infobox); the Eyuwan bases in Henan, Hubei and Anhui go in November 1934; the Sichuan-Shaanxi base is left in March 1935; the Zhejiang, Guangdong, Hunan and Guizhou soviets are gone by 1935 (ledger). The same shape is used for 1931

keyframe_review.note: 297,451 km2 for 1932-1935 against the page's 'approximately 70,000 square kilometers' for a population of over 3.4 million, 'at its peak in 1933': a ratio of 4.2, beyond a factor of two. Decision: the infobox figure is the Chinese Soviet Republic proper (the Ruijin core) and the shape is the sum of every soviet district the page names (Jiangxi, Minzhegan, Xianggan, Xiang'egan, Honghu, Xiang'echuanqian, Eyuwan, Eyushan, Shaanxi-Gansu, Sichuan-Shaanxi, Hailufeng; the page gives them no years), so the shape stands as the scattered soviets and the renderer should expect patches, not a block (the shape covers Jiangxi 40%, Fujian 27%, Chongqing 42%, Hubei 21%, Anhui 18%, Henan 17%). Only the years change: 1935 is a new keyframe because the Long March page ends the Jiangxi Soviet in 1934 and the Sichuan-Shaanxi base in March 1935.

correction.text: northern Shaanxi, the Soviet base that Mao's army reached in October 1935 and 'joined with local Communist forces there' (Cliopatria's 1936 shape)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the Long March year: Cliopatria draws the 1932 soviets through 1935 although the Jiangxi Soviet was abandoned in October 1934 and the Fourth Army left the Sichuan-Shaanxi base in March 1935. The 1936 shape (41,631 km2) is the base 'Liu Zhidan, Gao Gang, and Xu Haidong' had already set up in northern Shaanxi (the Shaan-Gan-Ning page dates the Shaan-Gan-Ning base area to 1934, closely paraphrased). The armies on the march hold no land.

41,631 km2 in northern Shaanxi (Yan'an, Suide and Bao'an inside it): the Bao'an and Yan'an Soviet. The infobox gives the Republic 'approximately 70,000 square kilometers' at its 1933 peak, ratio 0.59, within a factor of two. The Chinese Soviet Republic was 'dissolved on 22 September 1937' and became the Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region.

correction.text: unchanged shape minus Xinjiang (and a Qinghai sliver) and the strays of the same strip in Kazakhstan and Mongolia: what remains is the Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region on the Shaanxi-Gansu-Ningxia border with Yan'an and Suide, about 45,000 km2

keyframe_review.note: 1,622,107 km2 for 1938-1945, of which 96% of Xinjiang's cells (5,487 of 5,709) and only 158 cells (about 45,000 km2) in Shaanxi, where the Yan'an base lies. No page opened gives the Communists land in Xinjiang (the Civil War page mentions Xinjiang only for 1936); the Shaan-Gan-Ning page puts the Border Region on the Shaanxi-Gansu-Ningxia border and has the CCP taking control of the rich east, including Suide, in spring 1939 (closely paraphrased). Decision: the Xinjiang part is wrong and is removed. The other base areas (Jin-Sui, Jin-Cha-Ji, Ji-Lu-Yu) are named on that page but without years or areas, so they stay undrawn until the 1945 keyframe; a gap-filler should open their pages. [repair 2026-10-25] The first correction removed Xinjiang and Qinghai only and left 5 cells in Kazakhstan and 4 in Mongolia (193 cells); with {country Kazakhstan} and {country Mongolia} subtracted too, 184 cells remain, all in China.

correction.text: the Liberated Zone: 'By spring 1945, there were 19 Communist-governed areas in China in which 95 million people lived'; Cliopatria's 1947 shape (northern Shaanxi, Shanxi, Hebei, Shandong, Inner Mongolia) used as the nearest drawn outline

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page: the 'Liberated Zone' in 1945 'contained 19 base areas, including one-quarter of the country's territory and one-third of its population'; in fall 1945 the armies had 1.27 million men. One quarter of China is about 2.4 M km2 against the 607,731 km2 of the 1947 shape (ratio 0.25, beyond a factor of two): the quarter counts guerrilla and contested rural areas that no shape can show, so the proxy is a lower bound. The page does not list the 19 areas.

correction.text: the Liberated Zone of 1945-1946, as in Cliopatria's 1947 shape; the 1946 shape of 110,922 km2 is only the Yan'an region (northern Shaanxi and a part of Shanxi)

keyframe_review.note: 110,922 km2 is the Shaan-Gan-Ning region and a part of Shanxi, yet the page has the Communists governing 19 base areas in 1945 and full-scale war breaking out on 26 June 1946 between 'CCP and KMT forces'; the 1947 outline is the better 1946 shape. The page does not date the base areas' growth, so this is a reading of the 1945 figures (confidence 2). Yan'an stays inside until the KMT seized it in March 1947.

607,731 km2: northern Shaanxi, Shanxi, Hebei, Shandong and Inner Mongolia. Dated pegs: 'In March 1947, the KMT achieved a symbolic victory by seizing Yan'an' (still inside the shape: Cliopatria draws the year's outline) and 'On 30 June 1947, CCP troops crossed the Yellow River and moved to the Dabie Mountains area' (outside it). The shape also includes Taiyuan's surroundings although the page has the Taiyuan defenders overcome only on 24 April (1949).

2,247,136 km2: all of Manchuria (Liaoning, Jilin and Heilongjiang 99%), Shanxi 98%, Hebei 81%, Shandong 82%, Inner Mongolia 79% and Luoyang. The page dates the sequence: Luoyang fell 'by April 1948'; the Liaoshen campaign 'was launched on 12 September 1948', Jinzhou fell on 14 October, Changchun surrendered on 19 October and Shenyang fell on 1 November. Cliopatria draws the end-of-year outline; the ledger carries the months. Shanxi is drawn whole although Taiyuan fell only on 24 April 1949 (the page's date for the assault); the shape stands. Revised 2026-11-01 (fx-25): the keyframe stands (verdict ok); the 1948 snap of 7,403 cells came from a ledger that took the Northeast only from the Nationalists in November, leaving the countryside unowned. Ledger events added before it: the Northeast countryside by spring 1948 (Liaoshen campaign page) and Shandong on 24 September 1948 (Chinese Civil War page). Still without an event after this pass, about 1,000 cells of the 1948 shape (Hebei 526, Henan 209, Shaanxi 91, western Inner Mongolia 91, Shanxi 50): no page opened dates them.

2,785,265 km2 at the proclamation: the north, the northeast, Henan, Shandong, Jiangsu (88%), Anhui (66%) and Hubei (45%) after the Pingjin (to 31 January), Huaihai and Yangtze campaigns (21-23 April). The pages give no dated sentence on Shanghai, Hangzhou, Wuhan or the south before October; the KMT government 'retreated to Canton (Guangzhou) until 15 October, Chongqing until 25 November' and 'the majority of the resistance collapsed after the fall of Chengdu on 10 December 1949', which belong to people-s-republic-of-china. Unverified for the lower Yangtze provinces: page budget.

region.text: the Jiangxi-Fujian soviet area of the predecessor row plus a 100 km circle at Ruijin (116.03 E, the capital), which lies outside Cliopatria's 1930-1931 shape (it ends at 115.28 E)

ledger.note: 7 November 1931: Mao Zedong and Zhu De proclaim the Chinese Soviet Republic, with its capital at Ruijin. The Republic was 'proclaimed on 7 November 1931 by Chinese Communist Party (CCP) leaders Mao Zedong and Zhu De'; infobox capital 'Ruijin, Jiangxi Soviet (1931-1934)'. The page does not give the territory of the day; the core is the Jiangxi-Fujian soviet of the predecessor row plus a 100 km circle at Ruijin (the capital lies outside Cliopatria's 1930-1931 shape). The other soviets follow in the next event. [repair 2026-10-25: Ruijin added; the first draft used the predecessor shape alone.]

region.text: the other soviets the page names as territories of the Republic (Minzhegan, Xianggan, Xiang'egan, Honghu, Xiang'echuanqian, Eyuwan, Eyushan, Shaanxi-Gansu, Sichuan-Shaanxi, Hailufeng): Cliopatria's 1932 shape outside the Jiangxi-Fujian core

ledger.note: 7 November 1931: the Republic is proclaimed over the scattered soviets. The page lists the Minzhegan, Xianggan, Xiang'egan, Honghu, Xiang'echuanqian, Eyuwan, Eyushan, Shaanxi-Gansu, Sichuan-Shaanxi and Hailufeng soviets as its territories, says 'the second-largest soviet, in Eyuwan, failed to send delegates' to the founding conference and that 'Beginning in 1929, soviets began to be created in isolated regions across the country'. It dates none of them, so they are taken as standing on the day of the proclamation; the outline is Cliopatria's 1932 shape outside the core (1,040 cells), a reading (confidence 2). The republic-of-china dossier has no matching loss. [repair 2026-10-25: added, so that the growth from the 1931 core to the 1932 shape is not unexplained.]

region.text: the part of Cliopatria's 1932 shape in Jiangxi and Fujian: the Jiangxi Soviet around Ruijin, capital of the Chinese Soviet Republic

ledger.note: 1933: Chiang's fifth encirclement campaign opens against the Jiangxi Soviet. 'Most of its equipment was lost during Chiang's fifth encirclement campaign; this began in 1933'; the Republic 'reached its peak in 1933' with over 3.4 million people on about 70,000 km2. The page gives no month and no end date.

October 1934: the Communists abandon Ruijin and the Long March begins. 'On 10 October 1934 the CCP decided to abandon its Jiangxi Soviet and headquarters in Ruijin, Jiangxi'; the breakout attack came on 16 October near Yudu. The Chinese Soviet Republic infobox gives the start as 7 October 1934, the body 16 October: the pages disagree on the day. No fixed seat until Bao'an in 1936.

region.text: the part of Cliopatria's 1932 shape in Jiangxi and Fujian: the Jiangxi Soviet around Ruijin, capital of the Chinese Soviet Republic

ledger.note: 10 November 1934: Ruijin falls and the fifth encirclement campaign ends. Infobox 'Fall of Ruijin: 10 November 1934'; the Long March page speaks of prominent figures captured 'after the fall of Ruijin in November 1934'.

region.text: the part of Cliopatria's 1932 shape in Jiangxi and Fujian: the Jiangxi Soviet around Ruijin, capital of the Chinese Soviet Republic

ledger.note: 10 November 1934: the Jiangxi Soviet is lost with Ruijin. Infobox 'Fall of Ruijin: 10 November 1934'. The page names the Jiangxi Soviet, not a boundary; Jiangxi and Fujian are the reading. Two weeks later (30 November-25 December) the First Army fought the Battle of Xiang River (Long March page).

region.text: the part of Cliopatria's 1932 shape in Henan, Hubei and Anhui: the Eyuwan soviet and its neighbours

ledger.note: November 1934: the Eyuwan bases are lost. Eyuwan Soviet page: the Fourth Nationalist Encirclement Campaign 'defeated Eyuwan's Fourth Red Army in late 1932' (July-September 1932: 300,000 troops sent against it) and the infobox disestablishes the soviet in 1932; the text says the Communist bases 'continued to hold out well until late 1934' and that 'in November Xu Haidong was defeated and fled with the Twenty-fifth Red Army towards the Shaanxi-Sichuan base area'. The page does not resolve the 1932 and 1934 dates; the cells stay in the 1932 keyframe to 1934 because the holdouts did, and go in November 1934 (confidence 2: the month is the page's, the region is Cliopatria's outline in the three provinces). [repair 2026-10-25: added; the 1932 shape's Henan, Hubei and Anhui cells vanished by 1935 with no event.]

region.text: the part of Cliopatria's 1932 shape in Zhejiang, Guangdong, Hunan and Guizhou: the Minzhegan, Hailufeng and Hunan-based soviets

ledger.note: By 1935 (bridging; the page dates none of these soviets): the southern soviets are gone. Chinese Soviet Republic page: 'During the course of the next two years, Communist forces abandoned almost all of their soviets in southern China'; it gives no dates for the Minzhegan, Hailufeng, Xianggan, Xiang'egan or Honghu soviets. The 1935 keyframe holds only northern Shaanxi, so the year is the first without them. The Eyuwan Soviet page, opened for the Henan-Hubei-Anhui cells, is silent on these. [repair 2026-10-25: added.]

region.text: the part of Cliopatria's 1932 shape on the Sichuan-Shaanxi border (Chongqing, Sichuan, southern Shaanxi)

ledger.note: March 1935: the Fourth Red Army leaves the Sichuan-Shaanxi base. 'The Fourth Red Army under Zhang Guotao departs from its base on the Sichuan-Shaanxi border'; it was later largely destroyed by attacks of Chiang's forces and the Ma clique (closely paraphrased). The page does not say who held the base afterwards; the Nationalist Republic is the reading.

region.text: northern Shaanxi, the Soviet base of Liu Zhidan, Gao Gang and Xu Haidong

ledger.counterpart: Northern Shaanxi Soviet (Liu Zhidan, Gao Gang, Xu Haidong)
ledger.note: 19 October 1935: Mao's army reaches northern Shaanxi and joins the local Soviet. 'Finally, in October 1935, Mao's army reached Shaanxi province and joined with local Communist forces there'; 'The First Front Army arrived in Yan'an on 19 October 1935 with about 8,000 survivors' (timeline: Wuqizhen, 19 October). The Chinese Soviet Republic infobox says 22 October 1935; the local base under Liu Zhidan, Gao Gang and Xu Haidong had been set up earlier (Shaan-Gan-Ning page: the base area dates from 1934, closely paraphrased).
1936: the Communist seat is Bao'an. Infobox 'Bao'an, Yan'an Soviet (1936-1937)'; the Second Red Army 'reached Bao'an (Shaanxi) on October 22, 1936', ending the Long March for all forces.
January 1937: the CCP headquarters is established in Yan'an (Shaan-Gan-Ning page, closely paraphrased).

22 September 1937: the Chinese Soviet Republic becomes the Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region under the Second United Front. 'The Chinese Soviet Republic was dissolved on 22 September 1937'; the Yan'an Soviet was 'reconstituted officially as the Shaan-Gan-Ning' Border Region (a [citation needed] sentence), while the Shaan-Gan-Ning page has it 'officially established' by the Marco Polo Bridge incident of 7 July 1937: the pages disagree. Same state, same colour (rule 2).

region.text: the base areas behind Japanese lines in Shanxi, Hebei and Shandong, drawn as the part of Cliopatria's 1947 shape in those provinces (the 1945 proxy); no page lists their outlines

ledger.note: September 1937: the Red Army becomes the Eighth Route Army and fights in the Japanese rear. Eighth Route Army page: 'created from the Chinese Red Army on September 22, 1937' (a table in the article gives 25 August 1937); the army advanced into the Japanese rear 'establishing the Taihang resistance base area' shortly after the Marco Polo Bridge incident of 1937 (closely paraphrased). Chinese Civil War page: 'In occupied areas, the Communists established military and political bases from which it carried out guerilla warfare.' The pages name no other base area with a year, so the zone is the 1945 proxy in Shanxi, Hebei and Shandong (confidence 2: the month is the page's, the region is a reading). [repair 2026-10-25: added; the Second Sino-Japanese War was missing.]

region.text: Suide and the rich east of the Border Region

ledger.note: Spring 1939: the Border Region takes the rich east around Suide. In spring 1939 the KMT attacked and the CCP took control of the rich east, including Suide (page, closely paraphrased). Cliopatria's 1938 shape already holds Suide. The page also has the KMT blockade from 6 January 1941 and a repelled attack in March 1941.

region.text: the Liberated Zone: 19 Communist-governed areas

ledger.note: 1945: the Liberated Zone of 19 base areas. 'By spring 1945, there were 19 Communist-governed areas in China in which 95 million people lived'; the 'Liberated Zone' in 1945 'contained 19 base areas, including one-quarter of the country's territory and one-third of its population'. The page does not say when or where each was won (Jin-Cha-Ji, Jin-Sui and Ji-Lu-Yu are named on the Shaan-Gan-Ning page without years; the Eighth Route Army page dates only the Taihang base, 1937), so the date is bridging and the outline is Cliopatria's 1947 shape as a proxy. [repair 2026-10-25] Counterpart changed from republic-of-china to empire-of-japan: the page puts the bases 'in occupied areas', behind Japanese lines, from 1937 (see the contest of September 1937); the republic-of-china dossier has no 1945 loss to the Communists but ends the Japanese occupation of the same North China land in September 1945 (its ledger 69-77), so its occupation_end regions should leave out the base areas (note for ea-08-c).

region.text: the base areas behind Japanese lines in Shanxi, Hebei and Shandong, drawn as the part of Cliopatria's 1947 shape in those provinces (the 1945 proxy); no page lists their outlines

ledger.note: 10 October 1945: the fighting period of the Eighth Route Army against Japan ends on the page. Eighth Route Army page: its combat statistics cover 'From September 1937 to 10 October 1945'. Japan's surrender is not dated on the Chinese Civil War page; the empire-of-japan dossier dates it 2 September 1945 from the Second Sino-Japanese War page, so the contest here ends five weeks later than Japan's formal surrender, at the page's own date. [repair 2026-10-25: added.]

region.text: Manchuria: Heilongjiang, Jilin and Liaoning, 'the Northeast'

ledger.note: March 1946: the war for the Northeast begins. 'In March 1946, despite repeated requests from Chiang, the Soviet Red Army continued to delay pulling out of Manchuria', which led to full-scale war for the control of the Northeast; the page says the Communists 'received Northeastern China from the Soviets' and 'soon began taking surrenders from the Japanese'. The full-scale war between CCP and KMT broke out on 26 June 1946.

region.text: Yan'an, the CCP headquarters

ledger.note: March 1947: the Nationalists seize Yan'an. 'In March 1947, the KMT achieved a symbolic victory by seizing Yan'an, the capital of the Yan'an Soviet.' The page does not date the recapture; the Chinese Communist Party page says only that the KMT held 'cities such as Yan'an, the CCP headquarters, for much of the war'.

March 1947: the leadership leaves Yan'an. 'In March 1947, the KMT achieved a symbolic victory by seizing Yan'an'; the pages opened do not name the next seat (Beiping is the capital at the proclamation of 1 October 1949).

region.text: the Dabie Mountains area on the Henan-Hubei-Anhui border, reached on the march south of the Yellow River

ledger.note: 30 June 1947: the Communists cross the Yellow River into the Central Plains. 'On 30 June 1947, CCP troops crossed the Yellow River and moved to the Dabie Mountains area.' The page gives no dated fighting there until 'by April 1948, the city of Luoyang fell'.

region.text: most of Shanxi, outside Taiyuan and Datong (radii are readings), as the shanxi-clique dossier gives it

ledger.note: By October 1948 (bridging; the page dates the Central Shanxi campaign nowhere): most of Shanxi is Communist. Taiyuan campaign page: after that campaign 'the majority of the province had fallen into the communist hands' and the Nationalists were 'left with only two cities in entire Shanxi', Taiyuan and Datong; the campaign page's infobox starts the siege of Taiyuan on 5 October 1948, so 1948 is the latest year the page allows. Cliopatria's Shanxi cells go from 196 (1947) to 780 (1948). Mirrors shanxi-clique ledger 9. [repair 2026-10-25: added.]

union.text: eastern Inner Mongolia (Hulunbuir, Xing'an, Liaobei and Rehe), the part of the Northeast that lies in Inner Mongolia

intersect.text: Liaoning, Jilin, Heilongjiang and eastern Inner Mongolia

minus.text: the three Nationalist garrison cities, which fall in October-November (ledger 23-25)

region.text: the Northeast countryside: Cliopatria's 1948 shape in Liaoning, Jilin, Heilongjiang and eastern Inner Mongolia, without the garrison cities Shenyang, Changchun and Jinzhou

ledger.note: Spring 1948: the Communists hold the Northeast outside the garrison cities (no month given). Liaoshen campaign page: 'By spring 1948, the Communist forces were in control of the countryside across Northeast China', having 'seized control of the Jingha Railway, cutting off the Nationalist land route supply lines to Shenyang and Changchun' and isolated 'the Nationalist forces in Shenyang, Changchun and Jinzhou from each other'; the three cities stay out of this event and fall in ledger 23-25 (October-November). Counterpart nobody because the compiler showed these Northeast cells (Heilongjiang 2,134, Jilin 935, Liaoning 658, Inner Mongolia 2,493) with no owner in 1948: only the Nationalist-held cells were taken by the November gain below. Eastern Inner Mongolia is added as part of the Northeast on the researcher's reading: the Inner Mongolia page says the autonomous region 'was established in 1947, incorporating the areas of the former Republic of China provinces of Suiyuan, Chahar, Rehe, Liaobei, and Xing'an' and that it followed Communist victory in Manchuria, but gives no 1948 date for those leagues. Added fx-25, 2026-11-01.

region.text: the city of Luoyang

ledger.note: April 1948: Luoyang falls. 'By April 1948, the city of Luoyang fell, cutting the KMT army off from Xi'an.'

region.text: Shandong province, the part inside Cliopatria's 1948 shape

ledger.note: 24 September 1948: Jinan falls and Shandong passes to the Communists. 'Following a fierce battle, the CCP captured Jinan and Shandong province on 24 September 1948.' Chinese Civil War page, re-read 2026-11-01. Added fx-25: the ledger had no Shandong gain between the 1947 and 1948 keyframes (393 cells of the 1948 shape were unowned).

region.text: Jinzhou, taken in 24 hours

ledger.note: 14 October 1948: Jinzhou falls in the Liaoshen campaign. 'On 14 October, the Communists launched an all-out assault and captured the city in 24 hours.' The campaign 'was launched on 12 September 1948 and led by Lin Biao'.

region.text: Changchun, the garrison surrendered

ledger.note: 19 October 1948: Changchun surrenders. 'The siege of Changchun ended on 19 October when the Nationalist garrison surrendered.'

region.text: Shenyang and the rest of the Northeast held by the Nationalists

ledger.note: 1 November 1948: Shenyang falls and Manchuria is won. 'On 1 November, the Communists captured Shenyang.' The page does not use the word 'all', but the Northeast is Communist from here (the Cliopatria 1948 shape covers Liaoning, Jilin and Heilongjiang at 99%).

region.text: Manchuria: Heilongjiang, Jilin and Liaoning, 'the Northeast'

ledger.note: 1 November 1948: the fighting for the Northeast ends. The Liaoshen campaign (12 September) ends with 'On 1 November, the Communists captured Shenyang'.

region.text: the Beiping-Tianjin front, Hebei

ledger.note: 21 November 1948: the Pingjin campaign opens. 'The Pingjin campaign lasted 64 days, from 21 November 1948 to 31 January 1949.'

region.text: Beiping, Tianjin and Hebei

ledger.note: January 1949: Beiping and Tianjin pass to the Communists. 'In January 1949, Beiping changed hands through a negotiated settlement'; the campaign ended on 31 January. The page names Beiping only; Tianjin and Hebei are the reading from the campaign's name.

region.text: the Beiping-Tianjin front, Hebei

ledger.note: 31 January 1949: the Pingjin campaign ends. 'The Pingjin campaign lasted 64 days, from 21 November 1948 to 31 January 1949.'

region.text: east-central China secured in the Huaihai Campaign

ledger.note: Early 1949: the Huaihai campaign secures east-central China. 'The Huaihai Campaign of late 1948 and early 1949 secured east-central China for the CCP.' The page gives no dates or places of the battles; the Xuzhou area on the Huai is the reading.

region.text: the Central Plains front opened by the crossing of 30 June 1947

ledger.note: Early 1949: the Central Plains fighting ends with the Huaihai victory ('late 1948 and early 1949').

union.text: Jiangsu south of the Yangtze, crossed from 21 April

region.text: Nanjing and the lower Yangtze

ledger.note: 21-23 April 1949: the Yangtze is crossed and Nanjing falls. 'Mao rejected Stalin's position and on 21 April, began the Yangtze River Crossing Campaign'; 'On 23 April, they captured the KMT's capital, Nanjing.' The page gives no date for Shanghai, Hangzhou or Wuhan.

region.text: Taiyuan, Yan Xishan's capital of Shanxi, and Datong, the last two Nationalist cities in the province

ledger.note: 24 April 1949: Taiyuan is taken. 'In the early morning of April 24, with the support of more than 1,300 artillery pieces' the assault began and 'by 10:00, the Taiyuan defenders were completely wiped out'. The year is the section's, not the sentence's. [repair 2026-10-25] Counterpart changed from republic-of-china to shanxi-clique: Yan Xishan's Taiyuan is held by the shanxi-clique dossier (ea-08-x) until it dissolves into this state in April 1949 (its ledger 10). Datong is added as that dossier has it: the Taiyuan campaign page says the Datong garrison 'realized that it was all over after witnessing the nationalist defeat in Taiyuan' and surrendered, which puts it after 24 April 1949 but gives no date (confidence 2).

region.text: the communist-held land of 1949

ledger.note: 1 October 1949: Mao Zedong proclaims the People's Republic at Tiananmen Square. 'Mao Zedong officially proclaimed the People's Republic of China (PRC) with its capital at Beiping'; 'before a massive crowd at Tiananmen Square on 1 October 1949' (Chinese Communist Party page). The Communist state becomes the PRC, same land and party.

wars.name: Fifth encirclement campaign against the Jiangxi Soviet

zones.text: the part of Cliopatria's 1932 shape in Jiangxi and Fujian: the Jiangxi Soviet around Ruijin, capital of the Chinese Soviet Republic

wars.outcome: Nationalist victory: Ruijin fell on 10 November 1934 (infobox) and the Communists broke out of Jiangxi in October.
wars.note: The page says only that the campaign 'began in 1933' and that 'most of its equipment was lost' in it; the first four campaigns are not dated on the pages opened.

wars.name: Long March
wars.outcome: The Communist armies left Jiangxi (October 1934), fought at the Xiang, Wu and Jinsha rivers and reached northern Shaanxi in October 1935; the First, Second and Fourth Armies met again in October 1936.
wars.note: A retreat that holds no ground: Zunyi Conference 15-17 January 1935, Wu River 1 January 1935, Jinsha 29 April-9 May, Luding Bridge 29 May, Lazikou Pass 16 September; strength from about 100,000 to fewer than 7,000 of the original, 8,000 survivors at Yan'an.

wars.name: Second Sino-Japanese War

zones.text: the base areas behind Japanese lines in Shanxi, Hebei and Shandong, drawn as the part of Cliopatria's 1947 shape in those provinces (the 1945 proxy); no page lists their outlines

wars.outcome: Japan surrendered in 1945. The Communists, nominally inside the Nationalist army as the Eighth Route Army under the Second United Front, built base areas behind Japanese lines and held 19 of them, 95 million people, by spring 1945 (Chinese Civil War page).
wars.note: The republic-of-china dossier is an ally here, not an enemy, against Japan; the two fought each other again from 1939 in the Border Region (the war entry below) and in the Civil War. Dates: the Eighth Route Army page is 'From September 1937 to 10 October 1945' for fighting and 'created from the Chinese Red Army on September 22, 1937'; the Chinese Civil War page: 'From 1937 to 1945, hostilities were mostly put on hold as the Second United Front fought the Japanese invasion of China' and 'In occupied areas, the Communists established military and political bases'. The zone is the 1945 proxy for the base areas in Shanxi, Hebei and Shandong, since no page outlines them or dates them beyond the Taihang base (1937). [repair 2026-10-25: added.]

wars.name: Kuomintang attacks and blockade of the Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region

zones.text: Suide and the rich east of the Border Region

wars.outcome: The Communists took the rich east including Suide in spring 1939; the KMT banned aid on 6 January 1941 and tried to encircle the region; a KMT attack was repelled in March 1941.
wars.note: The Second United Front (the Xi'an Incident of December 1936 led to it, Chinese Communist Party page) is the background; the page dates the Japanese bombing of Yan'an from November 1938 to October 1941.

wars.name: Chinese Civil War

zones.text: Manchuria: Heilongjiang, Jilin and Liaoning, 'the Northeast'

wars.outcome: Communist victory: the People's Republic was proclaimed on 1 October 1949 and the Nationalist government left for Taiwan on 7 December 1949.
wars.note: Phase two of the war: 'full-scale war between CCP and KMT forces broke out on 26 June 1946' after the truce collapsed; the Soviet delay in Manchuria dates the war for the Northeast from March 1946.

wars.name: Liaoshen campaign

zones.text: Manchuria: Heilongjiang, Jilin and Liaoning, 'the Northeast'

wars.outcome: Communist victory: Jinzhou (14 October), Changchun (19 October) and Shenyang (1 November) taken; Manchuria won.
wars.note: 'Launched on 12 September 1948 and led by Lin Biao.'

wars.name: Pingjin campaign
wars.outcome: Communist victory: 'In January 1949, Beiping changed hands through a negotiated settlement.'

wars.name: Huaihai campaign
wars.outcome: Communist victory: it 'secured east-central China for the CCP'.
wars.note: The page dates it only 'late 1948 and early 1949'.

wars.name: Yangtze River Crossing campaign
wars.outcome: Communist victory: the crossing began on 21 April 1949 and Nanjing fell on 23 April.
wars.note: Taiyuan fell on 24 April (assault begun 'in the early morning of April 24').

certainty.note: Soviet districts held by guerrilla control, not by survey: the Jiangxi core is known by its capital, the other soviets by names without boundaries.
The Border Region and the 19 base areas of 1945 were rural districts behind Japanese lines; no boundary is on the pages.
Fronts moved campaign by campaign; only the cities (Yan'an, Luoyang, Jinzhou, Changchun, Shenyang, Beiping, Nanjing, Taiyuan) are dated.

sources.title: Chinese Soviet Republic
sources.note: Proclamation 7 November 1931, dissolution 22 September 1937, capitals, the 70,000 km2 peak of 1933, fall of Ruijin 10 November 1934, the fifth encirclement campaign. Repair pass: reopened for the soviets listed as the Republic's territories (none dated), Eyuwan's absence from the founding conference, the Ruijin capital, and the 'abandoned almost all of their soviets in southern China' sentence.

sources.title: Long March
sources.note: The abandonment of Jiangxi (10 October 1934), the Fourth Army's departure (March 1935), the arrival in northern Shaanxi (October 1935), Bao'an (22 October 1936).

sources.title: Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region
sources.note: Yan'an headquarters January 1937, the spring 1939 gain of Suide, the 1941 blockade, the loss of Yan'an in March 1947; thin on area, leaders and dissolution; other border regions named without years.

sources.title: Chinese Civil War
sources.note: The Liberated Zone of 1945, March 1946 Manchuria, June 1946 war, Yan'an March 1947, the 1947-1949 campaigns, the proclamation of 1 October 1949. Repair pass: reopened for 'In occupied areas, the Communists established military and political bases', the 19 base areas of spring 1945, and the Second United Front.

sources.title: Chinese Communist Party
sources.note: Founding (23 July 1921), Xi'an Incident, proclamation at Tiananmen; thin on the base areas (no Ruijin, Long March or Xibaipo).

sources.title: Eyuwan Soviet
sources.note: Repair pass: the Eyuwan soviet's defeat in late 1932 and the holdouts to November 1934 (Xu Haidong's Twenty-fifth Red Army); no area given.

sources.title: Eighth Route Army
sources.note: Repair pass: created from the Red Army on 22 September 1937 (table: 25 August); the Taihang base area of 1937; fighting period September 1937 to 10 October 1945; silent on Jin-Cha-Ji, Jin-Sui, Ji-Lu-Yu and Shandong bases and on the number of base areas.

sources.title: Taiyuan campaign
sources.note: Repair pass: infobox 5 October 1948 to 24 April 1949; after the undated Central Shanxi campaign the Nationalists held only Taiyuan and Datong; Taiyuan fell on 24 April 1949; Datong surrendered afterwards, undated.

sources.title: Liaoshen campaign
sources.note: fx-25 pass: 'By spring 1948, the Communist forces were in control of the countryside across Northeast China'; Jingha Railway seized; Shenyang, Changchun and Jinzhou isolated; no month and no list of cities held at the end of 1947.

sources.title: Inner Mongolia
sources.note: fx-25 pass: autonomous region established in 1947 on the areas of Suiyuan, Chahar, Rehe, Liaobei and Xing'an after the Communist victory in Manchuria; no 1948 or 1949 dates for the leagues.

notes: Budget 5 pages, all used (Chinese Soviet Republic, Long March, Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region, Chinese Civil War, Chinese Communist Party). ONE STATE OR TWO (Q17427): the Chinese Communists row (1928-1931, Jinggangshan and the Jiangxi base) and this row are one continuing party-state; chinese-communists (ea-08-c) ends on 7 November 1931 with this dossier as successor; the colour agent should give both the china family colour. TYPE: rebel (hatched in its own colour until the proclamation of the PRC on 1 October 1949); during the Second United Front the Border Region was nominally part of the Chinese war effort, which the pages do not turn into a vassal relation. RAISED FOR THE REVIEWER: (1) the 1938-1945 shape is Xinjiang (96% of its cells) plus the Yan'an region: Xinjiang is removed; (2) the 1932-1935 shape is 4.2 times the page's 70,000 km2 and kept as the scattered soviets; (3) the 1945 and 1946 outlines are the 1947 shape as a proxy for the 19 base areas, because no page lists them; (4) the leadership seat after the loss of Yan'an (March 1947) to the proclamation is not on the pages (Xibaipo is not among them); (5) no ruler strip: the pages give Mao Zedong as head of the Republic in 1931-1934 and Zhang Wentian for 1934-1937 (infobox), Mao as Chairman of the Politburo in 1943 and of the Central Committee in 1945, but nothing for 1937-1942. NOT ON THE PAGES: the dates of Zhangjiakou's capture (October 1946), Shijiazhuang, the recapture of Yan'an (the year is not given), Shanghai, Hangzhou, Wuhan, Xinjiang's 1949 change, the E-Yu-Wan soviet's end; the fall of Ruijin is the infobox's 10 November 1934, and the pages disagree on the start of the Long March (7, 10 or 16 October 1934) and on the arrival in Shaanxi (19 or 22 October 1935). Gazetteer names needed: Yan'an, Ruijin, Suide, Bao'an (Zhidan), Dabie Mountains (a region). Counterparts without dossiers: the Northern Shaanxi Soviet (a local base, absorbed in 1935). Mirror events in republic-of-china (ea-08-c) found: contest_start Manchuria (March 1946), gain of Yan'an (March 1947), contest_end and loss of Manchuria (November 1948), loss of Beiping and Tianjin (January 1949), of east-central China (January 1949) and of Nanjing (April 1949); missing there: Luoyang (April 1948), Taiyuan (April 1949), Jiangxi (November 1934), the Sichuan-Shaanxi base and Suide, which predate its keyframes or are small. REPAIR PASS 2026-10-25 (after the adversarial review of ea-08-d): (1) 1931 keyframe and found region: the predecessor row's 1930-1931 shape does not contain Ruijin and omits the soviets, so the 1931 keyframe is now Cliopatria's 1932 shape (it contains Ruijin) and the ledger carries the core (found, with a 100 km circle at Ruijin) and the other soviets (a gain from republic-of-china in the same month, confidence 2); republic-of-china (ea-08-c) has no matching loss. (2) Losses of the 1932 soviets: Henan, Hubei and Anhui in November 1934 (Eyuwan Soviet page, confidence 2) and Zhejiang, Guangdong, Hunan and Guizhou by 1935 (confidence 1, page silent). (3) Second Sino-Japanese War added (wars, with a contest with empire-of-japan from September 1937 to October 1945 over the base areas of Shanxi, Hebei and Shandong); the gain of the 19 base areas now names empire-of-japan, not republic-of-china. Note for ea-08-c and jk-01: the republic-of-china occupation_end and empire-of-japan occupation_end regions of September 1945 for Beiping, Tianjin, Hebei, Shandong and Shanxi should leave out the Communist base areas, and empire-of-japan has no contest or loss against this state. (4) Shanxi: Taiyuan and Datong (April 1949) now name shanxi-clique, and a 1948 gain of the rest of Shanxi (confidence 1) mirrors shanxi-clique ledger 9; shanxi-clique is a predecessor. (5) 1938 keyframe correction also removes Kazakhstan and Mongolia (184 cells). DISAGREEMENTS / LEFT OPEN: the Eyuwan Soviet page dates the soviet's end both to 1932 (infobox, and 'defeated Eyuwan's Fourth Red Army in late 1932') and to late 1934 (bases 'continued to hold out well until late 1934'); the dossier keeps the cells to November 1934. The ends of the Honghu, Minzhegan, Hailufeng and Xiang'e soviets are on no page opened. The Eighth Route Army, Civil War and Shaan-Gan-Ning pages date no base area but Taihang (1937), so the 19 base areas stay a 1945 proxy (Cliopatria's 1947 shape, which also contains Mongolian cells). Still open for a gap-filler: the 1948 gains of Inner Mongolia, Shandong and Hebei, the 1949 gains of Henan, Hubei, Shanghai and Xi'an, and the seats of Wayaobao (1935) and Xibaipo (1948). The repair pass opened three pages beyond the original budget of five (Eyuwan Soviet, Eighth Route Army, Taiyuan campaign) and reopened two of the five.
